extra_misconceptions.fact: Suffocating or burning a tick causes it to regurgitate infectious fluids into the bite; pull it straight out with fine-tipped tweezers.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Coating an embedded tick with petroleum jelly or touching it with a hot match forces it to back out safely.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Rubbing frozen tissue shreds cells with internal ice crystals; rewarm frostbite gently in 99 to 104 degree Fahrenheit water instead.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Vigorous rubbing of frostbitten toes restores blood circulation faster than warm water immersion.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Incising or sucking a snakebite damages nerves and introduces mouth bacteria; keep the limb immobilized at heart level and evacuate.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Cutting across a venomous snakebite and sucking out the venom reduces systemic toxin absorption on the trail.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Rebreathing into a bag worsens hypoxia at elevation or during asthma attacks; coach slow abdominal breathing and check for altitude illness.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Breathing into a paper bag is always the safest field treatment when a camper begins hyperventilating at high altitude.

extra_socratic_questions: Which physical indicator distinguishes life-threatening heatstroke from heat exhaustion during a steep afternoon hike?
What happens to a blister's infection risk when you drain fluid through the top dome instead of the base edge?
Why is it dangerous to rub frostbitten fingers or immerse them in hot water above 108 degrees Fahrenheit?
What cloud formation or barometric change confirms an approaching squall line before thunder becomes audible?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Even biodegradable soap pollutes water and strips fish mucus; carry wash water 200 feet away from any water source and scatter it in soil.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Biodegradable camp soap can be used directly inside a backcountry lake or stream without harming aquatic life.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Animals easily smell and dig up buried food scraps, which habituates wildlife to human campsites; pack out all organic trash and peels.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Burying leftover food scraps and fruit peels in a deep cathole speeds decomposition and hides food from wildlife.

extra_misconceptions.fact: New fire rings scorch soil and sterilize microbes for years; use a camp stove or an existing mound fire pan when fires are permitted.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Building a new rock fire ring at an unimpacted campsite leaves less trace than using a lightweight camp stove.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Unauthorized rock cairns disturb insect habitats and confuse off-trail navigation; leave rocks and natural objects exactly as found.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Stacking rock cairns along a well-marked trail helps hikers navigate while honoring Leave No Trace principles.

extra_socratic_questions: Under what condition should your patrol walk spread out rather than single file when traveling off established trails?
What distance measurement from lakes and streams confirms a cathole or dishwashing site meets Leave No Trace standards?
Why is it harmful to dig a trench around a pitched tent or clear pine needles down to bare mineral soil?
Where should a Scout hang odor-proof food bags or place bear canisters relative to the sleeping and cooking areas?

extra_misconceptions.fact: A compass needle aligns with local magnetic fields toward magnetic north, requiring declination adjustment to match true north map grids.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The red magnetic needle on a baseplate compass points directly to true geographic north on a topographic map.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Contour V-shapes pointing downhill mark a ridge or spur, whereas V-shapes pointing uphill toward higher ground indicate a stream drainage.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Contour lines that V-shape sharply toward lower elevation on a topographic map indicate a stream drainage or ravine.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Phone GPS chips receive satellite signals in airplane mode, though map tiles must be downloaded offline before leaving cellular coverage.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Smartphone GPS receivers require cellular tower coverage to calculate latitude and longitude coordinates in the backcountry.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Horizontal map distance ignores trail switchbacks and elevation gain; add one hour per 1,000 feet of ascent to horizontal pace estimates.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Straight-line map distance between two waypoints equals the actual walking distance across mountainous terrain.

extra_socratic_questions: Which contour pattern on a topographic map distinguishes a spur ridge from a stream valley or drainage gully?
What happens to your plotted hike path if you transfer a map bearing to a compass without magnetic declination adjustment?
What map measurements must your trek plan combine to estimate travel time using Naismith's rule in steep terrain?
Why is it dangerous to rely on a smartphone GPS app without offline map tiles and a magnetic baseplate compass?

extra_misconceptions.fact: An effective duty roster rotates cooking, water, and cleanup chores across all patrol members so everyone practices every camp skill.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Assigning the newest Scouts to wash dishes for every meal is a fair way to organize a weekend patrol duty roster.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Menu planning must verify every participant's dietary allergies and medical needs first to prevent anaphylaxis or hunger in the field.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The patrol grubmaster can finalize the weekend grocery list before checking food allergies or religious restrictions.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Sanitation crews should put the wash-water pot on the stove while the meal cooks so hot water is ready as soon as eating finishes.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Cleanup crews need to heat dishwashing water only after the entire patrol finishes eating the main course.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Webelos require shorter trek distances, closer adult supervision ratios, and age-appropriate pack weights tailored to their size and skill.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Webelos Scouts joining a troop campout can use the exact same backpacking mileage and gear load as older Scouts.

extra_socratic_questions: Why does a functional patrol duty roster rotate cooking and sanitation roles by meal rather than for the whole weekend?
What happens to campsite hygiene when the water and sanitation crew starts heating wash water only after the meal ends?
Which specific safety and dietary details must the patrol leader record when planning a campout with a Webelos den?
Where should the posted patrol duty roster and menu schedule be mounted in camp so every Scout can verify meal tasks?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Cotton absorbs sweat and rain like a sponge and conducts heat away from skin 25 times faster when wet, accelerating hypothermia.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Heavy cotton sweatshirts and denim jeans provide reliable warmth for cold-weather camping because the fabric is thick.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Long-term compression crushes down clusters and synthetic fibers, permanently reducing loft; store sleeping bags loose in a large cotton sack.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Keeping a sleeping bag tightly compressed inside its small trail stuff sack at home preserves the insulation shape.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Unbroken stiff boots cause severe friction blisters and hot spots; break in footwear on short local walks with trail socks before a trek.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Brand-new leather hiking boots are ready for a multi-day backpacking trek straight out of the retail box.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Trapped perspiration soaks inner layers from the inside out; open pit zips and remove insulation layers before exertion causes sweating.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Wearing a waterproof rain shell with all vents zipped shut during an uphill winter hike keeps you warmest and driest.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to the insulating R-value of a cotton base layer once sweat saturates the fibers during a winter hike?
Why should a hiker shed their fleece mid-layer before starting a steep climb while they still feel slightly cool?
Which boot fit check on an inclined ramp confirms your toes will not jam against the front cap on steep descents?
What damage occurs inside a synthetic or down sleeping bag stored tightly compressed in its stuff sack for months?

extra_misconceptions.fact: An exposed groundcloth catches rain runoff and channels water directly beneath the tent floor; fold all tarp edges completely under the tent.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Extending a ground tarp several inches outside the tent walls protects the tent floor better during a heavy rainstorm.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Even clear alpine streams carry microscopic Giardia and Cryptosporidium cysts from wildlife upstream; always boil, filter, or treat water.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Crystal-clear mountain stream water flowing from melting snowfields is pure enough to drink without any treatment.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Cryptosporidium has a tough outer shell that resists iodine and requires either boiling, a 1-micron filter, or four hours of chlorine dioxide.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Standard iodine or chlorine dioxide drops kill Cryptosporidium cysts within five minutes in icy backcountry water.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Storing a wet tent breeds mildew that permanently destroys polyurethane waterproof coatings and rots seam thread within days.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Rolling up a damp tent after a rainy campout and leaving it in its stuff sack until next month harms only the smell.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to rainwater pooling if your tent groundsheet or footprint extends three inches beyond the rainfly edge?
Which waterborne protozoan cyst resists standard chlorine tablets unless combined with microfiltration or boiling?
What boiling duration at high altitude confirms raw stream water is safe from viral, bacterial, and protozoan pathogens?
Where should a Scout check overhead and underfoot before staking a dome or A-frame tent in a wooded campsite?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Bottom-heavy packs pull your shoulders backward and strain your lower back; place dense gear mid-high and tight against the spine.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Heavy items like food bags and Dutch ovens belong at the very bottom of an internal-frame pack to lower the load.

extra_misconceptions.fact: The padded hip belt resting on your iliac crest should support 70 to 80 percent of the load, while shoulder straps mainly stabilize the pack.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A backpack's padded shoulder straps should carry the majority of the pack weight during an overnight trail hike.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Water seeps through backpack zippers and stitched seams during sustained rain; line the pack interior with a heavy-duty trash compactor bag.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Nylon backpack fabric is completely waterproof on its own and keeps a down sleeping bag dry during an all-day rain.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Swinging external gear shifts your center of gravity, snags on branches, and gets soaked by rain; pack equipment neatly inside the main bag.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Strapping sleeping bags, pots, and lanterns to the outside of a backpack improves balance on narrow brushy trails.

extra_socratic_questions: Where inside an internal-frame backpack should heavy patrol food and cooking pots be placed to protect your balance?
What happens to your center of gravity on rocky trails if heavy dense gear is packed low and far from your spine?
Which items must sit in top pockets or side pouches so your patrol can respond to sudden rain or a trail injury?
What hip-belt and shoulder-strap adjustment sequence confirms 70 to 80 percent of pack weight rests on your pelvis?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Camp stoves produce odorless carbon monoxide that causes fatal poisoning in enclosed spaces and can ignite nylon tent fabric in seconds.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Cooking inside a tent vestibule with the rainfly zipped protects the stove flame from wind without safety hazards.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Fuel vapor ignites explosively on hot metal; let the stove cool completely and move at least 20 feet from any flame before refueling.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Refilling a liquid-fuel stove while the burner crown is still hot saves time when boiling water for a large patrol.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Butane stops vaporizing near 31 degrees Fahrenheit and loses pressure in severe cold, while pumped white gas stoves work reliably in winter.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Upright isobutane canister stoves maintain strong burner pressure in subzero winter temperatures just like liquid fuel.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Enclosing a fuel canister inside a heat-reflecting windscreen overheats the pressurized cylinder and can cause a catastrophic stove explosion.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Wrapping a full aluminum wind screen tightly around an upright canister stove improves fuel efficiency safely.

extra_socratic_questions: Why is it dangerous to operate a canister or liquid-fuel stove inside a tent or zipped vestibule during a storm?
What happens to the vapor pressure inside an isobutane canister when ambient temperature drops below 20 degrees Fahrenheit?
Under what condition is it safe to unscrew the filler cap and pour white gas into a liquid-fuel camp stove tank?
What nutritional and weight differences distinguish a cold-weather backpacking menu from a warm-weather frontcountry menu?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Only one long-term camp counts for up to 6 nights, while each additional long-term trip adds at most 2 nights to the 20-night total.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Two 6-night summer camp weeks provide 12 qualifying nights toward the 20-night Camping requirement.

extra_misconceptions.fact: All 20 nights must take place at designated Scouting activities or events under the auspices of Scouts BSA.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Weekend family RV trips and non-Scouting backyard sleepovers count toward the 20 required camping nights.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Qualifying nights require sleeping under the stars or in a tent that you pitched, unless a council-provided summer camp tent is used.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Sleeping inside a permanent heated troop cabin during a winter campout counts as a qualifying camping night.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Only camping nights completed after registering in a Scouts BSA troop, Venturing crew, or Sea Scout ship count toward this badge.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Overnight family campouts completed as a Cub Scout automatically transfer into the 20-night Scouts BSA log.

extra_socratic_questions: Under what condition does a second week-long summer camp add two nights to your 20-night Camping total?
What distinguishes an eligible tent or open-sky overnight from a cabin stay in your 20-night camping log?
What specific logbook details verify that your 20 camping nights meet the long-term and short-term limits?
Why does pitching your own tent on short-term weekend campouts build stronger weather readiness than one summer camp?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Even biodegradable soap pollutes water sources unless greywater is carried at least 200 feet away and strained into soil.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Biodegradable camp soap breaks down immediately in lakes and streams without harming aquatic public health.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Buried food attracts bears and rodents to campsites and takes months to rot, so all food waste must be packed out in sealed bags.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Burying leftover food scraps and fruit peels in a fire ring feeds wildlife and leaves the campsite clean.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Outdoor citizenship and the Scout Law require keeping the patrol together, sharing shelter gear, and stopping early before panic sets in.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: True wilderness survival skill means pushing through storm hazards alone rather than slowing down for the group.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Preventing camp-wide illness requires scraping food, washing in hot soapy water, rinsing, and sanitizing in a third pot.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Quickly rinsing camp dishes in cold creek water kills foodborne bacteria across a patrol kitchen.

extra_socratic_questions: Where should a Scout position dishwashing sump holes and catholes relative to natural water sources to protect public health?
What separates personal hygiene practices like blister care from public health protocols like the three-pot dishwashing method?
Which physical indicators during a final campsite sweep confirm that your patrol upheld Leave No Trace and good citizenship?
Why is it dangerous to prioritize speed over the Scout Law when a patrol mate shows early signs of hypothermia on the trail?
